lesson_title: The Trial Balance: Two Columns That Must Agree
hook_text: A shop has R83 660 in the bank and still made a loss. The trial balance shows how.
clip_script: At the end of the month, call the register. Every account in the ledger answers with its balance. Debit family on the left: assets, expenses, drawings. Credit family on the right: capital, liabilities, income. Add both columns. Ridgeview Hardware: R140 250 on the left, R140 250 on the right. They agree, because every transaction went in once on each side. Now read it. Sales R27 600, cost of sales R18 400: gross profit R9 200. Add other income, take away rent, wages, telephone and bank charges, and the first month shows a loss of R6 240. But there is R83 660 in the bank! How? Most of it was the owner's capital and a loan. Money in the bank is not profit. And if your columns ever disagree, find the difference. If it divides by 9, two digits probably swapped places: 850 written as 580.
visual_style: A register-style list of accounts sliding into two columns, totals ticking up to matching figures, then a split screen of a full bank vault and a red profit figure.
mood: Revealing, careful, with a surprising twist.
pacing: Steady listing, a pause on matching totals, a twist on the loss, a quick detective tip.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the hidden error in a trial balance.
